answer: A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases therefore burns capital on every one it does not finish. Because the bridge deposit is held in the echo escrow, the shale audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 98 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
